html:
Paavo Nurmi was a Finnish distance runner, born in Turku in 1897, who won nine Olympic gold medals in the 1920s. He was called the Flying Finn.

He trained with a stopwatch in hand to keep an even pace, a new method then. At the Paris Olympics of 1924 he won five golds, two of them within about an hour. He set some twenty world records.

He was barred from the 1932 Olympics for taking money as an amateur. In 1952 he lit the flame at the Helsinki Olympics. For a young, poor country recovering from the civil war, his victories were a source of national pride, part of a wider tradition of Finnish distance running. See Finland and the modern Olympics.
sum: Paavo Nurmi was a Finnish distance runner, born in Turku in 1897, who won nine Olympic gold medals in the 1920s. He was called the Flying Finn.
